messages:
maya: Heads up — after the mkdocs migration some anchors are 404ing and a few headings lost their snippets. Looks like emoji in headings are causing slug collisions + redirects are duplicating. Example: build shows link -> /guides/#🚀-getting-started but the actual anchor is `getting-started`.
alex: ugh. reproable locally? can you paste the failing heading + the link that points to it?
maya: yup. here's the offending markdown:

maya: ```\n## 🚀 Getting started\nFollow these steps to spin up Redwood.\n```\n
maya: and from the docs index we have a link `[Getting started](./guides/#🚀-getting-started)` which used to work pre-migration.
kevin: seen this before with the mkdocs slugify change — emoji are being included in the fragment sometimes and the slugifier on deploy strips them differently. Two things we can do: (1) normalize headings to explicit IDs `## Title {#explicit-id}` as a safe migration; or (2) patch the slugify plugin to strip emoji consistently. Option (1) is fast but manual.
alex: for a quick hotfix can we run a small script that backfills explicit ids for headings that contain non-ascii? i can whip something up to add `{#...}` for those files and update links.
sophia: +1 for backfill. also we have duplicate redirects created by the old redirect map generator — it emits both `#%F0%9F%9A%80-getting-started` and `#getting-started` which confuses nginx. we should squash those into the canonical path.
mkdocs-ci: BUILD FAILED • 1 error
mkdocs-ci: Error: Link check failed — 1 broken fragment: /guides/#%F0%9F%9A%80-getting-started -> 404
maya: attaching quick grep output I ran:

maya: ```\n$ rg "^## .*🚀" docs/ | head\ndocs/guides/setup.md:12:## 🚀 Getting started\ndocs/tutorials/quickstart.md:5:## 🚀 Quickstart\n```\n
kevin: alex — if you want i can push a tiny mkdocs plugin that normalizes anchor generation to ascii-only and emits a canonical `data-anchor` attribute. that would avoid having to edit 50+ files.
alex: if plugin is non-invasive and covered by tests i'm fine with it. hotfix plan: (A) run linkcheck CI with `--strict-fragments` on a branch; (B) backfill explicit ids for the most critical pages; (C) land plugin in staging and run full linkcheck. who wants (B)?
maya: I can do (B) for the guides and tutorials I own. will open a PR with the `{#getting-started}` style ids and update inbound links.
kevin: created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/842 — plugin + unit tests. notes: handles emoji, ZWJ, and percent-encoded fragments.
sophia: once maya's PR lands i'll run the redirect-map generator with `--squash-duplicates` and push. also will add a small checklist to the migration guide so authors avoid inline emoji in headings when they want stable anchors.
maya: landed backfill for guides (ran locally + linkcheck) — PR 843. CI green on the subset.
alex: nice. i'll land the redirect squasher and drop a patch release to the docs site tomorrow AM. follow-up: we should add a docs linter rule to warn on emoji in headings and suggest explicit ids.
kevin: agreed. added issue to repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/229 — add linter + docs note.
maya: thanks all. leaving this thread open until the redirect squasher is live and anchor warnings are in place.
alex: thanks — :thumbsup:
